summary: A single-sweep 'N requests, 0 hits' claim was read as a durable fix for WordPress/mcp-adapter#332's per-request ability-registration-order bug; a fresh retest on the same build (7.1.2) reproduced the bug cleanly and repeatably via real REST requests
decision: method-failure — false negative from insufficient/wrong-shaped sampling
notes: 2026-09-22 comment on mcp-adapter#332 claimed 0 of the 3 [ERROR] lines over 44 requests on 7.1.2. 2026-09-24 retest: a bare wp-cli 'wp eval' reproduced it 0/6 times, but a real anonymous REST GET (/wp-json/wp/v2/posts) reproduced all 3 lines cleanly on 3/3 separate attempts, and 2 more bursts appeared during exploratory wp-cli calls whose bodies happened to load extra plugin classes. The trigger is tied to the rest_api_init bootstrap path (mcp-adapter hooks it at priority 15), which most bare CLI evals never exercise. Read via SFTP pull of logs/php/php-error.log (before/after diff), not wp debug.log (WP_DEBUG_LOG is off on this site).
